open_points.subject: Backup snapshot instant
open_points.text: State 3 says “a backup's instant is the one `store` reads when the copy's read transaction begins”; the changed rules say “the instant being that of the read that fixes its snapshot” and that the snapshot is fixed by the first audit-counter read.
open_points.question: Is the backup instant sampled when the read transaction is opened or when its first read fixes the SQLite snapshot?
options: When the read transaction is opened
When the audit-counter read fixes the snapshot
open_points.default_guess: Use the instant of the audit-counter read that fixes the snapshot, matching the changed A18 rule.

witness.initial: No backup read transaction exists, and an action is able to commit between opening one and its first read.
events: module:store opens the backup's read transaction.
An action commits a store change.
module:store performs the first read of the audit counter, fixing the snapshot.
outcomes: The backup records the earlier transaction-opening instant, as State 3's Time passage requires.
The backup records the later first-read instant, as changed A18 and the changed store ownership passage require.
witness.observer: The owner viewing the newest backup instant and any restore tooling reading the backup record.

set_aside.subject: WAL conversion followed by a later start failure
set_aside.text: “puts it in that mode when it is not” but, when a listener later fails, “an existing store is left as it was”
set_aside.question: If an existing store is changed to write-ahead-log mode and a later integrity, version, or listener check fails, must Registry restore its former journal mode, or may the failed start leave it in WAL mode?
options: Restore the former journal mode before stopping
Leave the store in WAL mode despite the failed start
set_aside.default_guess: Restore the former mode so the existing store is left as it was.

witness.initial: An existing valid store is not in WAL mode, and the owner-interface listener cannot be opened.
events: module:store successfully changes the existing store to WAL mode.
module:instance_lifecycle fails to open the owner-interface listener and stops the start.
outcomes: The store is restored to its former journal mode, as required by “left as it was.”
The store remains in WAL mode because the conversion succeeded and no rollback operation is stated.
witness.observer: The owner or the next Registry start inspecting the store's journal mode.

set_aside.subject: Temporary WAL store and SQLite sidecar files
set_aside.text: “a new store is made in write-ahead-log mode” while the flow removes or renames only “a file of the store's temporary name — … and no other file”
set_aside.question: How are the temporary database's WAL and shared-memory sidecar files handled before the temporary main database is renamed to the configured store name, and on an interrupted or failed start?
options: Checkpoint and close the temporary database so the main file is self-contained before renaming it
Rename or otherwise migrate the WAL sidecars with the main database
Permit sidecars under the temporary basename and define their cleanup and recovery
set_aside.default_guess: Checkpoint and close the temporary database before renaming the self-contained main file.

witness.initial: The configured store is absent, and creating its schema in WAL mode produces temporary-name WAL or shared-memory sidecars.
events: module:store creates the database under the temporary name and enables WAL mode.
Schema creation writes database state that may involve the temporary-name sidecars.
module:store completes or is interrupted while following the stated main-file rename and cleanup rules.
outcomes: The implementation checkpoints and closes first, then renames a self-contained main database and removes its sidecars.
The implementation renames only the main file or leaves temporary-name sidecars because the text permits touching only that named file.
witness.observer: The running instance or the next start, which may see missing committed schema state or leftover files.

set_aside.subject: Ordering of the snapshot-fixing database read and clock read
set_aside.text: “the read that fixes the snapshot — with the instant read from the clock at it”
set_aside.question: Because the clock read and the SQLite audit-counter read are separate operations, which one occurs first, and which event is the authoritative snapshot instant if a write commits between them?
options: Read the clock immediately before the audit-counter read
Perform the audit-counter read first, then read the clock
Define another explicit ordering or synchronization rule
set_aside.default_guess: Perform the audit-counter read first and sample the clock immediately afterward, treating the database read as the snapshot boundary.

witness.initial: A backup is starting and a write transaction is ready to commit.
events: module:store performs one of the clock read and audit-counter read.
The writer commits between those two operations.
outcomes: Clock-first records an instant before the commit while the snapshot may include the committed change.
Database-first may record an instant after the commit while the snapshot excludes that change.
witness.observer: The owner or restore tooling comparing the backup's recorded instant with the changes and audit sequence actually present in it.
